messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 4890012345 - gpu_capacity_critical in pool 'west-gpu-primary' — queue depth 1,150, avg wait 21s, autoscaler reports capacity_limit_reached
Anya: calling oncall-sre — Im on it. grabbing cluster metrics and recent job history.
Sam: Sam (oncall) here. autoscaler events show repeated 'scale blocked: fragmentation' and then 'max replicas reached'. pulling packer diagnostics.
Maria: Maria (runtime) flagged a MIG resize that ran overnight in multiple batches. possible mixed-slices left behind.
Sam: cluster events snippet:
```
Warning  FailedScheduling  30s  default-scheduler  0/46 nodes are available: 38 Insufficient gpu.mig.slices.
packer: cannot fit pod on any node due to mismatched slice footprints
```
Sam: autoscaler excerpt:
```
level=warn msg="cannot place due to fragmentation" fragmentation_score=0.82 desired_replicas=62
level=error msg="account quota reached" current=48 max=48
```
Leo: Leo (autoscale) joining. we hit a hard cloud quota; autoscaler tried but packer returned no viable packing because ~60% of nodes have inconsistent MIG partitions (mix of 1x16g, 2x8g, 4x4g).
Anya: customer impact list please.
support-bot: Affected customers: corp-zeta (latency spike ~2.2s -> 10s), start-up-gamma increased 5xxs ~7%, anonymous-free tier backlog up 12x.
Sam: region scope: west primary pool worst; east seeing spill but already high. routing prefers same-region; spilling is limited.
Maria: quick inventory: `rdwctl node show --pool west-gpu-primary --mig-summary` -> 46 nodes: 28 show non-uniform partitions.
Anya: mitigation options we can do immediately:
- create a temporary low-cost burst pool and update routing to spill lower-SLA traffic
- drain a controlled set of fragmented nodes after marking non-critical pods for eviction
- request emergency quota bump from cloud (will take time)
Which do we choose first?
Leo: burst-pool + spill routing is the fastest to reduce customer latency.
Sam: executing spill now:
```
rdwctl pool create burst-west --template=t4-burst --capacity=14
rdwctl routing update --source=west-gpu-primary --spill=burst-west --policy=non-sla
```
Sam: :white_check_mark: burst-west created and routing adjusted. queue depth fell from 1,150 -> 480 in ~5m.
Anya: good. next steps to reclaim stranded slots? can we evict safely?
Maria: prefer cordon+evict non-prod labeled pods only. if we touch prod pods we risk transient errors. I'll label a set of background-eval pods as evictable now.
Sam: cordoning nodes with label mig=stale and running controlled drains on 6 at a time. commands run:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-601
kubectl drain gpu-node-601 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```
Sam: observed some background models OOM during restarts; acceptable for eviction.
Leo: after the first wave of drains packer reports gains: 
```
packer: reclaimed 12 contiguous 8G-equivalent slots
autoscaler: desired 62 -> 54 (able to schedule more pods)
```
Anya: any surprises during drains?
Sam: noticed an older partitioning job left a mismatch where some nodes had 3x5g partitions patched to 4x4g but not cleaned; that caused wasted space.
Maria: Im starting a controlled repartition job on waves of 5 nodes: cordon -> repartition MIG -> uncordon. Will run health checks before proceeding to next wave. Dry-run pack predictions are promising.
Anya: customer comms drafted and sent to support: "Were seeing degraded throughput in west region due to GPU partitioning inconsistency and autoscaler capacity limits. Were routing non-SLA traffic to a temporary burst pool and performing rolling re-partitioning. Some requests may see elevated latency."
support-bot: Incident page created: INC-2026-03-15-west-gpu-capacity
Sam: timeline for incident so far:
```
02:10 UTC - batch MIG-resize job started (no pool lock)
08:55 UTC - marketing-driven traffic surge
09:01 UTC - queue alert fires; autoscaler fails to place due to fragmentation and quota
09:07 UTC - burst-west created and spill routing enabled
09:15 UTC - first cordon/drain wave initiated
09:32 UTC - packer shows reclaimed slots; queue trending down
```
Leo: follow-ups to prevent recurrence:
- add a pool-lock to any MIG-resize job so multiple batches do not create mixed state
- add fragmentation awareness into autoscaler decision function so it can trigger reparitioning or more aggressive evictions before hitting quota
- surface "packable slots" metric in alerts (not just queue depth)
Maria: I'll add a guard to the repartitioner to fail-fast when a node set would produce mixed partitions. I'll also prepare a script to detect and auto-tag 'mixed-mig' nodes nightly.
Anya: operational note: Sam will overlap on-call with Maria for 30 minutes while watch is ongoing, then handoff. Please collect logs, packer traces, and customer error windows for the postmortem.
Sam: handing off to Maria in 20m. I'll assemble a log bundle and provide packer trace graphs.
Maria: taking watch; will keep monitoring queue and routing stats. prepping postmortem skeleton assigned to eng-runtime + autoscale teams.
Anya: severity -> mitigated (monitoring). make sure we capture exact minutes of customer impact for SRE/Sales follow-ups.
support-bot: Incident state updated: mitigated -> monitoring. customers notified via status page.
Maria: final note before I take primary: we recovered without cloud quota increase by reclaiming stranded slots and using burst capacity. still need the policy fixes to avoid manual drains in the future.
Anya: thanks everyone. tight coordination and the spill pool prevented larger customer outages. watch for 2h, then rotate postmortem work.
Maria: will post the incident doc and evidence links in ~2h when stabilized. :white_check_mark:
